record.original_question: Let A be a purely inseparable form of the polynomial ring k^[n] over a field k, meaning that after base change to the perfect closure K of k it becomes isomorphic to K^[n]. If A is k-rational, i.e. Q(A) is isomorphic to k(n), or even if A is birationally contained in k^[n], must A already be trivial?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 1. Let A be a purely inseparable form of k[n], the polynomial ring in n variables over the ﬁeld k, i.e. A is isomorphic to K [n] over the perfect closure K of k. Is A trivial if A is k-rational, i.e. if the quotient ﬁeld L of A is isomorphic to k(n), or, more strongly, if A is birationally contained in k[n] ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $K$ denote its perfect closure. A finitely generated $k$-algebra $A$ is called a purely inseparable form of the polynomial ring $k^{[n]} = k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ if $A \otimes_k K \cong K^{[n]}$ as $K$-algebras. The form $A$ is called trivial if $A \cong k^{[n]}$ as a $k$-algebra. Let $Q(A)$ denote the field of fractions of $A$, and recall that $A$ is said to be $k$-rational if $Q(A) \cong k(x_1,\dots,x_n)$, and that $A$ is birationally contained in $k^{[n]}$ if $Q(A)$ embeds as a $k$-subalgebra into $k(x_1,\dots,x_n)$.

Question: Suppose $A$ is a purely inseparable form of $k^{[n]}$ such that $A$ is $k$-rational (or, more strongly, such that $A$ is birationally contained in $k^{[n]}$). Must $A$ then be trivial, i.e., isomorphic to $k^{[n]}$ as a $k$-algebra?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface related works (Asanuma's study of purely inseparable forms of the affine line; Kambayashi's triviality of separable $\mathbb{A}^2$-forms; ongoing work on separable $\mathbb{A}^3$-forms), but no source directly resolves the question of whether a $k$-rational (or birationally embedded in $k^{[n]}$) purely inseparable form of $k^{[n]}$ must be trivial. The status is not clearly established from the search.

status_evidence.title: On separable A2 and A3-forms
status_evidence.snippet: Separable A2-forms over k are trivial (Kambayashi); existence of nontrivial separable A3-forms is open. Nontrivial purely inseparable A1-forms exist (Asanuma).
status_evidence.claim: Closely related triviality questions about forms of polynomial rings remain partially open; no resolution of the k-rational purely inseparable case is cited.

status_evidence.title: Birational splitting and algebraic group actions
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of birational invariants of forms of affine space.
status_evidence.claim: Related framework but does not settle the stated question.
